tools.name: read_board
tools.description: Read a shared Excalidraw board and open it. Returns its shapes and the URL where anyone can watch and edit it live. Leave out board to start a new one.

tools.name: draw
tools.description: Draw on a board: boxes (rectangle, ellipse, diamond), text, arrows between two shapes, and frames that hold shapes under a name. Everyone with the board open sees it at once. Give shapes your own short ids to join them with arrows and put them in frames in the same call. Leave out x and y, and the b

tools.name: erase
tools.description: Erase shapes from a board by id. An arrow attached to an erased shape stays, so erase it too if it should go. The shapes in an erased frame stay.

tools.name: sync
tools.description: For the board's page: send the Excalidraw elements it changed and where its pointer is. With since, also receive the elements changed elsewhere and everyone else's cursors.

tools.name: put_image
tools.description: For the board's page: store the file of an image on the board, as a data URL.

tools.name: get_image
tools.description: For the board's page: read the file of an image on the board, as a data URL. Without one, the board has no such file.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "excalidraw" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_board, get_image · Private data: put_image, get_image · Public sink: sync.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_board, get_image · Private data: put_image, get_image · Public sink: sync

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
